name: King Pedro
description: King Pedro is a variant of the popular American card game Pedro (also known as Cinch or 63), played primarily in the northeastern United States and Canada. It adds the King of trumps as an additional scoring card worth 5 points, making the total points available 19 per hand instead of the standard 14. It is a trick-taking game where the 5 of trumps (the Pedro) and the 5 of the same color (the Left Pedro) are the most valuable cards.

history.origins: Developed from the 19th-century American game Pedro (also called Cinch or Double Pedro). The addition of the King as a scoring card was a regional variation that emerged in the northeastern United States and parts of Canada.
timeline: Mid-1800s: Original Pedro game develops from Pitch in the United States
Late 1800s: Pedro becomes extremely popular across the US
Early 1900s: Regional variants like King Pedro emerge in the Northeast
Present: Still played in parts of Canada and the northeastern US
history.cultural: Pedro and its variants were extremely popular in the US at the end of the 19th century. While its popularity declined in the 20th century, it remains beloved in specific regions including southern Louisiana, parts of Canada, and the northeastern US.
history.evolution: King Pedro represents one of several 'augmented' Pedro variants where additional scoring cards were added. Other variants include Sixty-three (63) and Eighty-three (83), which add even more scoring cards.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards to each player, 3 at a time. The turn to deal passes to the left after each hand.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 62 or more points by winning tricks containing valuable cards.
rules.gameplay: The high bidder leads to the first trick. If a trump is led, players must play a trump if possible. If a non-trump is led, players must follow suit or trump if possible. Highest trump wins the trick; if no trumps, highest card of led suit wins. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Deal 9 cards each (3 at a time); dealer rotates left. One round of bidding from dealer's left; minimum bid 7, maximum 14; must bid higher or pass; dealer forced to bid 7 if all pass. High bidder names trumps; everyone discards all non-trumps face down; dealer replenishes others to 6 cards and takes remainder (all trumps) for own hand. High bidder leads; follow suit or trump when possible; highest trump wins trick, else highest of led suit; winner leads next. First team to 62 or more points wins; bidder goes out rule when both teams 55+.

strategy.basic: The Pedro (5 of trumps) and Low Pedro (other 5 of same color) are worth 10 points togetherâ€”more than half the available points. Prioritize capturing or protecting these cards.
strategy.intermediate: When bidding, consider not just your trumps but whether you have protection in side suits. A hand with the two Pedros and a few other trumps is strong even without the Ace or King.
strategy.advanced: The King of trumps adds 5 points, making it as valuable as a Pedro. If you hold the King and several other trumps, you have a strong hand for bidding. Watch for situations where you can force opponents to play their Pedros by leading high trumps.
tips: If you have more than 6 trumps after the discard, you must play multiple cards to the first trick (burying the extras)
The Low Pedro can be a surpriseâ€”remember which suit is the same color as trump
In close games, remember the 'bidder goes out' rule: if both teams are near 62, the bidding team wins if they make their bid
Don't forget the trump Twoâ€”it scores 1 point for the team that was dealt it
